Determine whether the loan meets the stated §11.5 requirements for a property listed for sale in the last six months.

### Other documents

- Title commitment
- Appraisal report

- There is no subordinate financing.

Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Treat the property as listed for sale under §11.5 if it was listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date. Whether §11.5 applies to Platinum Select unchanged is part of Q-13.

Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a property meeting the trigger, verify that it is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for an investment property, verify that the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant; verify qualification as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI, with the program's channel minimum DSCR applying (Wholesale 1.0 and Correspondent 1.2) and the DTI alternative unresolved as Q-14. Verify a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves; a fully amortizing term; maximum LTV / CLTV of 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing; and required impounds. Interest only is not available.

Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the six-month trigger applies and whether every applicable stated characteristic is met. Do not resolve the stated Q-13 or Q-14 questions without confirmation.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The property was listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date, for the §11.5 requirements to apply.

- Twenty-four (24) months of reserves are provided.
- The loan has a fully amortizing term and is not interest only.
- LTV / CLTV is no more than 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
- There is no subordinate financing.
- Impounds are provided.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: If §11.5 applies, the property meets every applicable stated characteristic; if the six-month listing trigger does not apply, this job does not apply.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: The six-month listing trigger applies and any applicable stated characteristic is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: The property was not listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

requirements.requirement_text:
# For an entity borrower, verify the required entity documentation and the applicable document-specific requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Establish whether the entity borrower has provided the required entity documentation.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Entity documents

## Step
Initial Document Review: For an entity borrower, review the entity documents. Verify a complete, legible Certificate of Formation / Articles of Organization and all amendments. Verify a complete, legible Operating Agreement for LLCs and Partnerships, or Bylaws for corporations, with all referenced exhibits and amendments. The Operating Agreement or Bylaws must state whether the entity is member or manager managed, contain authorization to borrow money and enter into contracts for mortgage assets, and designate signers. Verify documentation evidencing ownership interests: for LLCs and Partnerships, the Operating Agreement must identify by name all persons with their ownership interest, or attach that information as an exhibit, or provide membership interest certificates / units in compliance with the Operating Agreement. For S or C Corporations, verify shareholder / stockholder certificates that comply with the Bylaws, if any, or the stock ledger if certificates are lost or unavailable; the certificate or ledger must account for all outstanding shares noted in the formation document, including those held by the corporation. If stock certificates are lost, destroyed, mutilated, or otherwise unavailable, verify an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate. For S-corporations or Partnerships where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, verify the most recent preceding tax year's K-1 statement for all members with 20% or more interest and a letter from the CPA or Tax Preparer affirming current ownership interest, with a statement to that effect if the preceding year's taxes have not been filed.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Verify that names on entity documents match the identification; if they do not match exactly, verify a letter of explanation addressing the discrepancy. Verify a Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date. If the entity is formed in a state other than where business is performed or where the property is located, verify a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted. Verify IRS Form SS4 or a Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter for the entity. An EIN exception request may be submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds. Verify a Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution signed by all members regardless of their percentage of interest, authorizing the transaction with Acra Lending and identifying who is authorized to sign the loan documents on behalf of and to bind the entity. Check whether it is required by the Operating Agreement or Bylaws even where ownership is held by one individual. It cannot designate a signor on a personal guarantee, only an authorized signor for the loan documents signed by the entity. If a Power of Attorney is used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, verify that it is utilized by the principal; see §23.5(C), not reproduced (Appendix B).

## Step
Validation and Verification: Do not accept borrower letters stating that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents. If the formation documents and the Operating Agreement or Bylaws conflict, additional information may be required. Legal reserves the right to condition for additional supporting documentation as determined in its sole discretion.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether all required documentation applicable to the entity and the stated document-specific requirements have been verified, and identify any outstanding conditions or additional information requested.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The complete, legible formation document and all amendments are provided.
- The applicable Operating Agreement or Bylaws and all referenced exhibits and amendments meet the stated requirements.
- The applicable documentation evidencing ownership interests is provided and meets the stated requirements.
- The applicable corporate share documentation is provided and meets the stated requirements, including an Affidavit of Lost Stock Certificate when required.
- For an S-corporation or Partnership where both stock certificate and stock ledger are unavailable, the required K-1 statements and CPA or Tax Preparer letter are provided.
- Entity document names match identification, or a letter of explanation addresses any exact-name discrepancy.
- A Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent valid within ninety (90) days of the closing date is provided.
- If applicable, a Certificate of Foreign Qualification or other qualification to operate in the state where business is being conducted is provided.
- IRS Form SS4 or a Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter is provided, or an EIN exception request with a letter of explanation stating the applicable grounds is submitted for review by Acra's Legal Department.
- The required Unanimous Written Consent / Board Resolution is provided and meets the stated requirements.
- If a Power of Attorney is used to designate an attorney in fact to execute a personal guarantee, it is utilized by the principal.
- No borrower letter states that required documents are not required, available, or excused from providing such documents.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The borrower is an entity borrower and every applicable check holds, with no outstanding required documentation or requested condition.
- **Conditional**: The borrower is an entity borrower and documentation or additional supporting documentation remains outstanding for a condition.
- **Fail**: The borrower is an entity borrower and a required check does not hold, including where required documentation is not provided.
- **Not Applicable**: The borrower is not an entity borrower.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Review the listing period, appraisal value, and transaction against the stated requirements for a property listed for sale in the last six months. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether a loan on a property listed for sale in the last six months meets the stated appraisal-based maximum LTV/CLTV and related loan characteristics.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Appraisal report
- Listing history

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report and listing history for appraised value, the last date listed, and the lowest recent listing price.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: If the property meets the listing-period test, verify that the loan meets the stated characteristics: the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s); for investment properties, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant; the loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI; a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is present unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; twenty-four (24) months of reserves are present, with cash-in-hand considered if otherwise consistent with the Guide; the term is fully amortizing and not interest only; maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is present; and impounds are present.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the listing-period test and all applicable stated loan characteristics are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The property has been listed for sale in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, the property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
- For an investment property meeting the listing-period test, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, the loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years is present unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, twenty-four (24) months of reserves are present, and cash-in-hand is considered only if otherwise consistent with the Guide.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, the loan has a fully amortizing term and is not interest only.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, no subordinate financing is present.
- For a property meeting the listing-period test, impounds are present.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The listing-period test is met and every applicable listed-property loan characteristic is met.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: The listing-period test is met and any applicable listed-property loan characteristic is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: The property has not been listed for sale in the last six months under the stated measurement.

# Review property type, transaction purpose, location, and CLTV against the stated property-type caps and above-80.00% LTV eligibility restriction. - Base Version

## Purpose

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Appraisal report

Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal report for property type and any property-specific classification relevant to the printed caps.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Identify the property type, transaction purpose, and whether the property is in Florida or LTV is above 80.00%.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify the applicable printed cap: Non-Warrantable Condo — 80% purchase, 75% refinance R/T, 75% refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties and Min DSCR: 1.0; Condotel / PUDtel — 75% purchase, 70% refinance R/T, 65% refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties and Min DSCR: 1.0; 2-4 Unit — Max CLTV: 80%; Manufactured Home — 65% purchase, 60% refinance R/T, 60% refinance C/O. Verify that above 80.00% LTV only SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome and PUD are eligible.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the applicable printed cap and above-80.00% LTV eligibility restriction are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- For a Non-Warrantable Condo, CLTV does not exceed 80% for purchase, 75% for refinance R/T, or 75% for refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties; Min DSCR: 1.0.
- For a Condotel / PUDtel, CLTV does not exceed 75% for purchase, 70% for refinance R/T, or 65% for refinance C/O, with -5% CLTV for Florida properties; Min DSCR: 1.0.
- For a 2-4 Unit property, CLTV does not exceed Max CLTV: 80%.
- For a Manufactured Home, CLTV does not exceed 65% for purchase, 60% for refinance R/T, or 60% for refinance C/O.
- Above 80.00% LTV, the property is only SFR, Warrantable Condo outside of Florida, Townhome or PUD.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The applicable property-type cap, its printed conditions, and the above-80.00% LTV eligibility restriction are met.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: An applicable property-type cap or printed condition is not met, or a property above 80.00% LTV is not one of the eligible property types.

- **Not Applicable**: The borrower has no bankruptcy or foreclosure.

# Verify that the entity provides IRS Form SS4 or a Federal Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) or Employer Identification Number (EIN) issuance letter. - Base Version

## Purpose

- An ITIN holder relying on the Foreign National Program resides outside of the U.S.

- **Pass**: The requirements applicable to the borrower’s citizenship type are met.
- **Conditional**: Required residence or authorization information has not yet been obtained or verified.

Do not resolve the stated “FICO 700” ambiguity without Acra confirmation.

- For “FICO 700”, purchase CLTV is no greater than 70%.
- For “FICO 700”, refinance — R/T and cash-out CLTV is no greater than 65%.
- For “FICO 660 to 699”, purchase CLTV is no greater than 65%.
- For “FICO 660 to 699”, refinance — R/T and cash-out CLTV is no greater than 60%.
- For “FICO 640 to 659”, purchase CLTV is no greater than 60%.
- For “FICO 640 to 659”, refinance — R/T and cash-out CLTV is no greater than 60%.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The applicable printed tier’s maximum CLTV is met, and any applicable Acra confirmation concerning the “FICO 700” tier has been obtained.
- **Conditional**: The applicable tier or CLTV has not been verified, or applicable Acra confirmation concerning the “FICO 700” tier remains outstanding.

# Verify the minimum DSCR required by each applicable situation stated in the guidelines. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether a calculated DSCR meets the stated minimum for each applicable situation.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Appraisal report
- Lease agreement
- Rent roll
- Loan application (1003)
- Credit report

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the DSCR calculation and information identifying the loan amount, credit file, property, occupancy, purpose, and borrower status.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Identify each applicable situation: LTV above 80.00%; loan amount over $2,000,000; 1 or no score / deficient tradelines; rural / unique property; non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel; first-time homebuyer; vacant-property rate & term refinance; vacant-property cash-out refinance; property listed for sale within six months; or mixed use, adult care or assisted living.

## Step
Validation and Verification: Verify the calculated DSCR against each applicable stated minimum: 1.20 for LTV above 80.00%; 1.0 for loan amount over $2,000,000; 1.1 for 1 or no score / deficient tradelines; 1.00 for rural / unique property; 1.0 for non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel; 1.150 for first-time homebuyer; 1.000 for vacant-property rate & term refinance; 1.15 for vacant-property cash-out refinance; 1.0 for property listed for sale within six months; and 1.2 for mixed use, adult care or assisted living.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether the calculated DSCR meets every minimum that applies. The stated DTI alternatives for vacant-property rate & term refinance and properties listed for sale are not resolved here; Acra confirmation is requested on those provisions.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If LTV is above 80.00%, calculated DSCR is at least 1.20.
- If the loan amount is over $2,000,000, calculated DSCR is at least 1.0.
- If there is 1 or no score / deficient tradelines, calculated DSCR is at least 1.1.
- If the property is rural / unique, calculated DSCR is at least 1.00.
- If the property is a non-warrantable condo or condotel / PUDtel, calculated DSCR is at least 1.0.
- If the borrower is a first-time homebuyer, calculated DSCR is at least 1.150.
- If the property is vacant and the transaction is a rate & term refinance, calculated DSCR is at least 1.000.
- If the property is vacant and the transaction is a cash-out refinance, calculated DSCR is at least 1.15.
- If the property was listed for sale within six months, calculated DSCR is at least 1.0.
- If the property is mixed use, adult care or assisted living, calculated DSCR is at least 1.2.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: A calculated DSCR is established and meets every applicable minimum listed in the checks.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: A calculated DSCR is below an applicable minimum, or an applicable minimum cannot be established as met.
- **Not Applicable**: None of the listed situations applies.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Calculate the DSCR using the qualifying rent and PITIA inputs specified in the guidelines. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine the calculated DSCR for a file qualifying using a calculated DSCR.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Lease agreement
- Rent roll
- Appraisal report

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the rental-income and property-expense information used for the calculation.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the file qualifies using a calculated DSCR, rather than No Ratio DSCR.

## Step
Validation and Verification: Calculate DSCR by dividing the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent by the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, homeowner's / condominium association fees, and subordinate financing, if applicable. Use the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

## Step
Final Determination: Record the calculated DSCR. Do not calculate a DSCR for a No Ratio DSCR file. The guidelines do not resolve which payment enters the denominator for an interest-only loan.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- For a file qualifying using a calculated DSCR, the calculated DSCR divides the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent by annual PITIA, including subordinate financing if applicable.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The file qualifies using a calculated DSCR and the calculated DSCR follows the stated formula.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: The file qualifies using a calculated DSCR and the calculation does not follow the stated formula, or required calculation inputs are not established.
- **Not Applicable**: The file qualifies as No Ratio DSCR, where no ratio is calculated.

values.skill: Verify the specified rental-income receipt and lease evidence when actual rents exceed market rents.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the specified rental-income receipt and lease evidence when actual rents exceed market rents. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the documentation stated for actual rents exceeding market rents is present.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Bank statement
- Lease agreement

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the actual-rent and market-rent information, rental-income receipt evidence, and lease agreement(s).

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether actual rents exceed market rents.

## Step
Validation and Verification: If actual rents exceed market rents, verify two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt and lease agreement(s) to continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing. Do not count a Security Deposit towards receipt; rents cannot be prepaid.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether the stated evidence and lease conditions are met. The guidelines do not select between the formula using the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent and the provision allowing use of the higher of actual or market rents.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If actual rents exceed market rents, two (2) consecutive months proof of rental income receipt is documented, lease agreement(s) continue at a minimum of three (3) months after closing, no Security Deposit is counted towards receipt, and rents are not prepaid.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Actual rents exceed market rents and all stated documentation and lease conditions are met.
- **Conditional**: Actual rents exceed market rents and required proof or lease documentation is outstanding.
- **Fail**: Actual rents exceed market rents and the stated receipt or lease conditions are not met.
- **Not Applicable**: Actual rents do not exceed market rents.

values.skill: Verify that required rent-schedule evidence is present for a single-family DSCR file or when proposed rental income is used to qualify.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that required rent-schedule evidence is present for a single-family DSCR file or when proposed rental income is used to qualify. - Base Version

## Purpose

Verify the required Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule or the stated short-term-rental replacement.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Appraisal report

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal and rental-income evidence in the file.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the property is single family on a DSCR qualifying file, the transaction is a lease-option purchase using excess monthly rent contributions for the required down payment, or proposed rental income is being used to qualify.

## Step
Validation and Verification: For a single-family property, verify that a Single-Family Comparable Rent Schedule (FNMA Form 1007) is present. For a property occupied as a short-term rental, an STRpro or similar appraisal form may replace a 1007 if signed by an appropriately licensed appraiser. A 1007 may be from the original appraiser or any state licensed appraiser.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether the applicable rent-schedule requirement is met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- A 1007 is present when required for a single-family DSCR qualifying file, a lease-option purchase using excess monthly rent contributions for the required down payment, or when proposed rental income is used to qualify, unless the stated short-term-rental replacement applies.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The applicable rent-schedule requirement is met, including the stated short-term-rental replacement when applicable.
- **Conditional**: Required rent-schedule evidence or verification is outstanding.
- **Fail**: Required rent-schedule evidence is not provided or does not meet the stated requirements.
- **Not Applicable**: None of the stated circumstances requiring a rent schedule applies.

values.skill: Determine whether the stated rent loss insurance requirement applies to the subject property and identify the stated CLTV/LTV overlap that requires confirmation.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Determine whether the stated rent loss insurance requirement applies to the subject property and identify the stated CLTV/LTV overlap that requires confirmation. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether six (6) months' rent loss insurance is required for the subject property under the stated property, LTV, and rent-qualification conditions.

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the case information for the subject property's number of units, occupancy subtype, CLTV, and DSCR qualification method.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Establish whether the property is a one- to four-unit, non-owner-occupied income property; establish whether LTV is > 70% and subject property rents are used to qualify. The stated requirement includes No Ratio DSCR.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Check whether the loan has ≤ 70% CLTV. If LTV is at or below 70% while CLTV is above 70%, preserve the stated unresolved case for Acra confirmation.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the rent loss insurance requirement applies, does not apply, or cannot be determined without Acra confirmation or missing trigger information.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The subject property has one to four units.
- The subject property is non-owner occupied.
- The subject property is an income property.
- The subject property's LTV is > 70%.
- Subject property rents are used to qualify.
- The loan has ≤ 70% CLTV.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The property and qualification conditions for the stated requirement are established, and the LTV/CLTV information does not present the stated unresolved overlap.
- **Conditional**: The trigger information is incomplete, or LTV is at or below 70% while CLTV is above 70%; establish the missing information or obtain the requested Acra confirmation before determining applicability.
- **Fail**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Not Applicable**: The stated property and qualification conditions for the rent loss insurance requirement are not met, or the loan has ≤ 70% CLTV and the stated LTV/CLTV overlap does not apply.

values.skill: Verify the required rent loss coverage or, when it cannot be obtained, the permitted reserve substitute.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the required rent loss coverage or, when it cannot be obtained, the permitted reserve substitute. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the rent loss insurance requirement is met by six (6) months' coverage or by the stated reserve substitution when the coverage cannot be obtained.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Hazard insurance declarations

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review hazard insurance declarations for rent loss coverage and its duration.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Confirm that the rent loss insurance requirement applies, using the Rent Loss Insurance Applicability determination.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that rent loss insurance covers rental losses incurred during the period the property is being rehabilitated following a casualty. If six (6) months' coverage is not provided, establish whether the required coverage cannot be obtained and whether reserves provide two (2) months for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether the required coverage or permitted reserve substitution is established.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Rent loss insurance covers rental losses incurred during the period the property is being rehabilitated following a casualty.
- The hazard insurance evidence establishes six (6) months' rent loss insurance coverage.
- Required rent loss insurance cannot be obtained.
- Reserves provide two (2) months for every one (1) month of rent loss coverage not provided.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The requirement applies and six (6) months' rent loss insurance coverage is established, or the required coverage cannot be obtained and reserves provide two (2) months for every one (1) month of coverage not provided.
- **Conditional**: The requirement applies, but the coverage, inability to obtain coverage, or reserve substitution has not yet been established; obtain the missing evidence or reserves information.
- **Fail**: The requirement applies and neither six (6) months' coverage nor the permitted reserve substitution is established.
- **Not Applicable**: The Rent Loss Insurance Applicability determination establishes that the requirement does not apply.

values.skill: Calculate the DSCR using the specified rent numerator and PITIA denominator, including subordinate financing when applicable.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Calculate the DSCR using the specified rent numerator and PITIA denominator, including subordinate financing when applicable. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine the DSCR using the calculation rule in STD-3.1 and the first-payment rule in STD-3.2.

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Identify the rent, payment, PITIA, and, if applicable, subordinate-financing data needed for the calculation.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Use the first payment due under the terms of the Note and include annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, homeowner's / condominium association fees, and subordinate financing if applicable in the denominator.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Calculate the DSCR only when the required calculation inputs and market-rent method are available; otherwise identify the unresolved inputs or reference.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The numerator is the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent.
- The denominator is the sum of annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees (PITIA), with subordinate financing included if applicable.
- The calculation utilizes the first payment due under the terms of the Note.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The DSCR is calculated using the required numerator, denominator, and first-payment basis, with the required inputs and market-rent method available.
- **Conditional**: The calculation is pending required inputs or the unavailable §14.14 market-rent method.
- **Fail**: A calculation is made using a numerator, denominator, or payment basis that does not meet the checks.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

values.skill: For allowable subordinate/secondary financing that is a HELOC, use the greater of the credit line limit or current credit line balance for CLTV eligibility.

requirements.requirement_text:
# For allowable subordinate/secondary financing that is a HELOC, use the greater of the credit line limit or current credit line balance for CLTV eligibility. - Base Version

## Purpose

Apply the stated HELOC CLTV calculation rule when subordinate/secondary financing is allowable.

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Identify whether the subordinate/secondary financing is a HELOC and obtain its credit line limit and current credit line balance.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply this rule only when the subordinate/secondary financing is allowable.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Compare the credit line limit with the current credit line balance and use the greater amount for CLTV eligibility.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the greater amount as the HELOC CLTV basis for eligibility.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- For allowable subordinate/secondary financing that is a HELOC, CLTV for eligibility is calculated on the greater of the credit line limit or current credit line balance.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The financing is allowable subordinate/secondary financing that is a HELOC, and the greater of the credit line limit or current credit line balance is used for CLTV eligibility.
- **Conditional**: The financing may be subject to this rule, but its allowable status or required credit-line data has not been established.
- **Fail**: The financing is allowable subordinate/secondary financing that is a HELOC, but the greater of the credit line limit or current credit line balance is not used for CLTV eligibility.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

values.skill: Obtain Acra confirmation of which payment enters the DSCR denominator for an interest-only loan.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Obtain Acra confirmation of which payment enters the DSCR denominator for an interest-only loan. - Base Version

## Purpose

Resolve the payment-basis question identified for interest-only loans in STD-3.2.

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Determine whether the loan is interest-only.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: For an interest-only loan, identify the unresolved question of which payment enters the DSCR denominator.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Obtain Acra confirmation of the payment basis for the DSCR denominator on an interest-only loan.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record whether that confirmation has been obtained; do not select a payment basis without it.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Acra confirmation identifies which payment enters the DSCR denominator for an interest-only loan.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: For an interest-only loan, Acra confirmation of the DSCR denominator payment basis has been obtained.
- **Conditional**: The loan is interest-only and the requested Acra confirmation has not been obtained.
- **Fail**: A payment basis is selected for an interest-only loan without the requested Acra confirmation.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

values.skill: Confirm whether subordinate financing is allowable for the program, lien type, and transaction, and apply the listed-for-sale prohibition.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Confirm whether subordinate financing is allowable for the program, lien type, and transaction, and apply the listed-for-sale prohibition. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether subordinate financing may be used, subject to the stated prohibition and the requested Acra confirmation.

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Identify whether subordinate financing is proposed and the relevant lien type and transaction.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Do not allow subordinate financing on a property listed for sale.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For other cases, obtain Acra confirmation of whether subordinate financing is allowed on this program and for the relevant lien types and transactions.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the proposed subordinate financing is prohibited, confirmed allowable, or remains subject to confirmation.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Subordinate financing is not used on a property listed for sale.
- Acra confirmation establishes whether the proposed subordinate financing is allowed on this program for the relevant lien type and transaction.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Subordinate financing is proposed, the property is not listed for sale, and Acra confirmation establishes that it is allowed for the relevant program, lien type, and transaction.
- **Conditional**: Subordinate financing is proposed, the property is not listed for sale, and the requested Acra confirmation has not yet established whether it is allowed.
- **Fail**: Subordinate financing is used on a property listed for sale, or Acra confirmation establishes that the proposed financing is not allowed.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

values.skill: Apply the stated loan-amount-dependent CLTV caps and DSCR minimum.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Apply the stated loan-amount-dependent CLTV caps and DSCR minimum. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the loan meets the additional loan-amount conditions below $200,000 and above $2,000,000.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Loan application (1003)

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and underwriting qualification for loan amount, purpose, CLTV, and DSCR.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: For a loan amount < $200,000, apply maximum CLTV 80% for purchase and 75% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out. For a loan amount > $2,000,000, apply minimum DSCR 1.0 or greater.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify each applicable cap or minimum against the loan's values.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether all applicable additional loan-amount conditions are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If loan amount is < $200,000, CLTV does not exceed 80% for purchase or 75% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out.
- If loan amount is > $2,000,000, DSCR is 1.0 or greater.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable additional loan-amount condition is met.
- **Conditional**: The DSCR result or transaction-purpose classification needed to apply a condition remains outstanding.
- **Fail**: An applicable CLTV cap or DSCR minimum is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: Neither loan-amount condition applies.

values.skill: Determine whether the borrower's citizenship category is among the published eligible types.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Determine whether the borrower's citizenship category is among the published eligible types. - Base Version

## Purpose

Identify whether the borrower has an eligible citizenship type and the applicable category-specific documentation requirements.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Loan application (1003)

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and relevant borrower documentation for citizenship or residency category.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Confirm whether the category is US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, or ITIN.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a Permanent Resident, verify an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89. For a Non-Permanent Resident, verify proof of legal residency, which may include an unexpired employment authorization document (EAD) or valid visa.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the eligible category and whether its stated documentation requirement is met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The borrower is a US Citizen, Permanent Resident, Non-Permanent Resident, Foreign National, or ITIN holder.
- A Permanent Resident has an unexpired PRA ID and SSA card / SSA-89.
- A Non-Permanent Resident has proof of legal residency.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The borrower has a listed eligible citizenship type and any applicable documentation requirement is met.
- **Conditional**: The borrower has a listed eligible citizenship type, but applicable proof of residency or Permanent Resident documentation remains to be obtained.
- **Fail**: The borrower does not have a listed eligible citizenship type, or an applicable documentation requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

values.skill: Verify that the subject property is an eligible property type and apply its printed cap where applicable.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that the subject property is an eligible property type and apply its printed cap where applicable. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the property type is eligible and whether its stated CLTV cap is met.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Appraisal report
- Loan application (1003)

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the appraisal_report and loan_application for property type, units, location, purpose, and CLTV.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Confirm the property type is SFR, Townhome, PUD, Warrantable Condo, Non-Warrantable Condo, Condotel / PUDtel, 2-4 Units, or Manufactured.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply the printed caps: Non-Warrantable Condo 80% purchase / 75% refinance and minimum DSCR 1.0; Condotel / PUDtel 75% purchase / 70% refinance rate & term / 65% refinance cash-out and minimum DSCR 1.0; 2-4 Unit maximum CLTV 80%; Manufactured Home 65% purchase / 60% refinance. Apply the Florida -5% CLTV adjustment for Non-Warrantable Condo and Condotel / PUDtel. Apply rural / unique property maximum CLTV 80% purchase / 75% refinance rate & term / 70% refinance cash-out, minimum FICO 700, and minimum DSCR 1.00. Above 80.00% LTV, only SFR, Warrantable Condos outside of Florida, Townhome and PUD are eligible.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the property type is eligible and every applicable printed condition is met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The property type is among the published eligible property types.
- The applicable printed property-type CLTV cap is met.
- For a Non-Warrantable Condo or Condotel / PUDtel, the applicable minimum DSCR is met.
- For rural / unique property, the minimum FICO and minimum DSCR are met and the applicable CLTV cap is met.
- If LTV is above 80.00%, the property is SFR, a Warrantable Condo outside of Florida, Townhome, or PUD.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The property is an eligible type and every applicable printed property-type requirement is met.
- **Conditional**: Evidence needed to establish property type, rural / unique status, DSCR, FICO, or transaction purpose remains outstanding.
- **Fail**: The property type is not eligible or an applicable printed property-type requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

values.skill: Verify that the subject property is not located in the ineligible state.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that the subject property is not located in the ineligible state. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the subject property's state is eligible under the published location restriction.

Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and appraisal_report for the subject property's location.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Compare the subject property's state with the published ineligible state, SD.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Validate the state shown for the subject property.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the property is outside SD.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The subject property is not located in SD.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The subject property is not located in SD.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: The subject property is located in SD.

values.skill: Verify the stated entity-form, formation, and ownership-structure requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the stated entity-form, formation, and ownership-structure requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether an entity borrower and its entity structure meet the stated entity eligibility requirements.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Entity documents
- Title commitment
- Loan application (1003)

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review entity_documents and the loan_application for entity type, formation and base, purpose, assets, ownership, and title-holding entities.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that the entity is a permitted type, US formed and based, and not a foreign-owned entity; verify that an entity borrower is an SPE engaged in owning and operating residential investment or rental properties and has no assets other than residential investment or rental properties.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that all entities holding direct ownership of the subject property are borrowing entities; exclude Cooperatives, Irrevocable Trusts, Land Trusts, IRAs, Non-Profit, and Joint Ventures; verify that nesting is limited to one (1) wholly-owned subsidiary owned by individual(s).

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the entity borrower and structure meet the stated requirements.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The entity is an allowed entity type and is US formed and based, and is not foreign owned.
- The entity borrower meets the stated SPE description and is not a series LLC.
- Every entity holding direct ownership of the subject property is a borrowing entity.
- The structure is not a prohibited entity type and does not exceed the stated nesting limit.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every stated entity eligibility and structure requirement is met.
- **Conditional**: Entity documents or evidence needed to establish a stated entity requirement remain outstanding.
- **Fail**: The entity type, formation, SPE status, title-holding structure, or nesting structure does not meet a stated requirement.
- **Not Applicable**: The borrower is not an entity borrower.

values.skill: Verify the stated entity guarantor and ownership-change requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the stated entity guarantor and ownership-change requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether required guarantees and the prior-homeownership attestation are present for an entity borrower.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Entity documents
- Loan application (1003)

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and entity_documents for direct and indirect ownership, guarantor identities, guarantees, homeownership attestation, and ownership changes.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Verify that all individuals with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provide a recourse guarantee, Acra approved or Exhibit 7; multiple guarantors' recourse is joint and several.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify that at least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience and that at least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer. If prior home ownership is not evident within the loan file, the underwriter may condition for supporting documentation. Verify that ownership changes intended to circumvent required personal guarantors are not recognized if made within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable guarantees, attestation, and ownership-change requirements are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- Every individual with direct or indirect ownership ≥ 20% provides the required recourse guarantee.
- At least one guarantor has prior homeownership experience.
- At least one borrower / guarantor attests on the application that they are not a first-time homebuyer.
- An ownership change intended to circumvent required personal guarantors made within 30 days prior to an Application Date or throughout the application process is not recognized.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable guarantee, attestation, and ownership-change requirement is met.
- **Conditional**: Required guarantee or homeownership evidence remains outstanding, including supporting documentation the underwriter conditions for.
- **Fail**: An applicable guarantee or attestation requirement is not met, or a disallowed ownership change is relied on to avoid required personal guarantors.
- **Not Applicable**: The borrower is not an entity borrower.

values.skill: Verify the definition and all stated DSCR conditions for a first-time homebuyer.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the definition and all stated DSCR conditions for a first-time homebuyer. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether a first-time homebuyer meets the program's stated DSCR conditions.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Loan application (1003)
- Credit report
- Bank statement

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application, credit_report, and supporting loan records for all applicants' homeownership history and the loan terms.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Apply the definition that all Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Verify minimum 700 FICO, maximum 70% CLTV, minimum DSCR of 1.150, maximum loan amount of $1,000,000, full amortization with no interest-only programs, impounds, and minimum six months reserves.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the first-time homebuyer definition and all applicable DSCR conditions are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- All Applicants have never previously owned a home (real property).
- FICO is at least 700.
- CLTV does not exceed 70%.
- DSCR is at least 1.150.
- Loan amount does not exceed $1,000,000.
- The loan is fully amortizing and is not interest-only.
- Impounds are required.
- Reserves are at least six months.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The first-time homebuyer definition and every stated DSCR condition are met.
- **Conditional**: The borrower meets the definition, but evidence or a stated condition remains outstanding.
- **Fail**: The first-time homebuyer definition or any stated DSCR condition is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: The applicants do not meet the definition of a first-time homebuyer.

values.skill: Verify the stated Foreign National eligibility requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify the stated Foreign National eligibility requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether a Foreign National meets the stated residence and transaction-purpose requirements and apply the published CLTV limits.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Loan application (1003)
- Credit report

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application and supporting borrower documentation for residence, authorization to live or work in the U.S., and transaction purpose.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the stated Foreign National requirements are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The borrower resides outside of the U.S.
- The borrower is not authorized to live or work in the U.S.
- The transaction is for a business purpose (investment property).
- The applicable CLTV does not exceed 70% for purchase or 65% for refinance — rate & term and cash-out.
- The loan is priced at FICO equal to 700.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every stated Foreign National eligibility requirement is met.
- **Conditional**: Required evidence or clarification of the borrower's residence, authorization, transaction purpose, or pricing remains outstanding.
- **Fail**: A stated Foreign National eligibility requirement is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: The borrower is not a Foreign National.

values.skill: Verify interest-only product, amount, FICO, CLTV, and restriction requirements.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify interest-only product, amount, FICO, CLTV, and restriction requirements. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether an interest-only loan meets the applicable published product and eligibility conditions.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Loan application (1003)
- Credit report
- Appraisal report

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review the loan_application, credit_report, and appraisal_report for interest-only term, product, loan amount, FICO, CLTV, and property and borrower characteristics.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Confirm the selected product is one of the published eligible interest-only products: 5 Yr / 30 year term on 5/1 or 7/1 ARM; 5 Yr / 30 Year Fixed; or 10 Yr / 40 Year Term.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Apply minimum loan amount $250,000 and minimum 640 credit score. For 10 Yr / 40 Year Term, also apply maximum 80% LTV / CLTV and maximum $3M loan amount. Interest-only is not available to first-time homebuyers, on vacant-property refinances, or on properties listed for sale.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable interest-only product conditions are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The selected interest-only product is a published eligible product.
- The loan amount is at least $250,000 and FICO is at least 640.
- For 10 Yr / 40 Year Term, loan amount does not exceed $3M and LTV / CLTV does not exceed 80%.
- The borrower is not a first-time homebuyer.
- The loan is not a refinance of a vacant property.
- The property is not listed for sale.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every applicable interest-only eligibility condition is met.
- **Conditional**: Product or loan evidence needed to determine an applicable interest-only condition remains outstanding.
- **Fail**: The product is not eligible or an applicable interest-only requirement or restriction is not met.
- **Not Applicable**: The loan is not interest-only.

values.skill: Verify that the subject is an eligible investment property.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that the subject is an eligible investment property. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the subject meets the program's investment-property occupancy requirement.

## Reference Documents

### Other documents
- Loan application (1003)
- Lease agreement

## Purpose

Determine whether a property listed within the stated period meets the applicable loan conditions.

- Loan application (1003)
- Appraisal report
- Bank statement

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Review listing_history, loan_application, appraisal_report, and relevant lien and underwriting records for listing dates, occupancy, value, and loan terms.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Treat a property as listed for sale if it was listed in the last six months, measured from the last date of being listed to the Application Date.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: For a covered loan, verify that the property is not in default or delinquent on liens; an investment property is tenant-occupied and not vacant; qualification is ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI; PPP is at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties; reserves are twenty-four (24) months; the loan is fully amortizing and not interest only; maximum LTV / CLTV is 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price; no subordinate financing is allowed; and impounds are required.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Determine whether the applicable listed-property conditions are met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The property was listed for sale within the last six months as measured from the last listing date to the Application Date.
- The property is not in default or otherwise delinquent on lien(s).
- For an investment property, the subject is occupied by a tenant and is not vacant.
- The loan qualifies as either ≥ 1.0 DSCR or 43% maximum DTI.
- The loan has a prepayment penalty of at least three (3) years unless the property is in a state that does not allow prepayment penalties.
- Reserves are twenty-four (24) months.
- The loan is fully amortizing and is not interest only.
- LTV / CLTV does not exceed 65% based on the lesser of appraised value or lowest recent listing price.
- No subordinate financing is allowed and impounds are required.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The property is listed within the stated period and every applicable listed-property condition is met.
- **Conditional**: Evidence or a condition needed to determine or clear an applicable listed-property requirement remains outstanding.
- **Fail**: An applicable listed-property condition is not met.

values.skill: Calculate DSCR using the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator and the specified annual payment and expense amounts as the denominator.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Calculate DSCR using the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator and the specified annual payment and expense amounts as the denominator. - Base Version

## Purpose

Calculate DSCR with annual real estate taxes included in the denominator.

## Step
Step 1 - Initial Document Review: Gather the data needed for the DSCR calculation: annual in-place rent, market rent, the annual denominator amounts, and the first payment due under the terms of the Note. Identify whether the loan is interest-only.

## Step
Step 2 - Eligibility Verification: Use the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent as the numerator. Include annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees in the denominator; include subordinate financing if applicable.

## Step
Step 3 - Validation and Verification: Divide the numerator by the denominator. If the loan is interest-only, obtain Acra confirmation of which payment enters the denominator. Apply the market rent reference §14.14 only when its applicable method is available; it is not reproduced in the excerpt.

## Step
Step 4 - Final Determination: Record the DSCR only when the required amounts and applicable calculation basis are available. Do not treat the subordinate-financing calculation rule as establishing that subordinate financing is permitted.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The numerator is the lesser of annual in-place rent or market rent.
- The denominator includes annual principal, interest, real estate taxes, property insurance, and homeowner's / condominium association fees.
- Subordinate financing is included in the denominator if applicable.
- The DSCR is the numerator divided by the denominator.
- The first payment due under the terms of the Note is used, subject to Acra confirmation of the payment basis for an interest-only loan.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every step is met and every check holds, with the applicable market rent method and, for an interest-only loan, Acra confirmation available.
- **Conditional**: The calculation is subject to obtaining data needed for the formula, the applicable §14.14 market rent method, or Acra confirmation of the denominator payment basis for an interest-only loan.
- **Fail**: A step is not met or a check does not hold, including when the calculation omits annual real estate taxes from the denominator.
- **Not Applicable**: There is no case for this outcome.

# Verify that documents signed outside the U.S. use an allowed acknowledgment method and meet the title company's acceptance requirement. - Base Version

## Purpose

## Step

Final Determination: Record whether the applicable acknowledgment route and title company acceptance requirements are met.

- If documents were signed outside the U.S. before a U.S. embassy or consular official, the certificate of acknowledgement includes the embassy or consular seal.

- For documents signed in a Hague Convention country, the title company accepts the acknowledgment and apostille.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: No documents were signed outside the U.S., or the applicable notarization route, required acknowledgment details, and title company acceptance are satisfied.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that the trust file includes a complete, legible Trust copy or a Certification of Trust containing each required statement. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the required trust document or certification and all listed trust details are present.

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the complete, legible Trust copy or Certification of Trust.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the file contains one of those document forms.

## Step
Validation and Verification: Verify that the document states the existence and date of the Trust; Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s); Trustee powers; revocability and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke; names and number of Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust; Trust identification number (a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number); how title to Trust assets should be taken; and that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether the Trust document or Certification of Trust is complete, legible, and includes every required item.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- A complete, legible copy of the Trust or a Certification of Trust is provided.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states the existence and date of the Trust.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states the Trustor(s) and current Trustee(s).
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states the powers of the Trustee.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states whether the Trust is revocable and, if revocable, who holds the right to revoke.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states the names and number of the Trustees required to sign on behalf of the Trust.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states the Trust identification number, which is a Social Security number or an IRS-issued Tax Identification Number.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states how title to the Trust assets should be taken.
- The Trust document or Certification of Trust states that the Trust has not been revoked, modified, or amended in any manner.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: A complete, legible Trust copy or Certification of Trust is provided and every required statement is present.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: The Trust copy or Certification of Trust is missing, incomplete, illegible, or omits a required statement.
- **Not Applicable**: Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that the trust is valid under its state's law, revocable, established by natural persons during their lifetime, and has the required primary beneficiary. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the trust meets the stated validity, revocability, establishment, and primary beneficiary requirements.

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the Trust or Certification of Trust for governing state, revocability, trustors, effective date, and beneficiaries.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Verify that the Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established; is revocable; was established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly; and became effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.

## Step
Validation and Verification: Verify that the primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether every stated trust structure requirement is met.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The Trust is valid under the laws of the state in which it is established.
- The Trust is revocable and can be changed or canceled at any time for any reason during a Trustor's lifetime.
- The Trust was established by one or more natural persons, solely or jointly.
- The Trust became effective during the lifetime of the person(s) establishing it.
- The primary beneficiary of the Trust is the individual(s) establishing the Trust.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every check holds.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: The Trust is invalid under the law of the state in which it is established, is irrevocable, was not established by one or more natural persons, did not become effective during the establishing person's or persons' lifetime, or does not have the establishing person or persons as primary beneficiary.
- **Not Applicable**: Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

values.skill: Verify that the Trust specifies the required Trustee powers, beneficiary consent terms, and protections of lender rights.

requirements.requirement_text:
# Verify that the Trust specifies the required Trustee powers, beneficiary consent terms, and protections of lender rights. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the Trust contains all required terms concerning mortgage authority, beneficiary consent, risk, and lender rights.

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the Trust for provisions concerning Trustee authority, beneficiary consent, lender risk, and creditor rights.

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the Trust specifies that the Trustee has power to hold title and mortgage the property.

## Step
Validation and Verification: Verify that the Trust specifies either that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money or that consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage; that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights; and that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether all required terms are specified.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- The Trust specifies that the Trustee has the power to hold title and mortgage the property.
- The Trust specifies that the beneficiary does not need to grant written consent for the Trust to borrow money, or that such consent has been granted in writing for purposes of the mortgage.
- The Trust specifies that there is no unusual risk or impairment to the lender's rights.
- The Trust specifies that holding title in the Trust does not diminish the lender's rights as a creditor.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: Every check holds.
- **Conditional**: There is no case for this outcome.
- **Fail**: Any check does not hold.
- **Not Applicable**: Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.

# Verify that written exception by Acra Senior Management is obtained when the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same. - Base Version

## Purpose

Determine whether the required written exception is present when the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) differ.

## Step
Initial Document Review: Review the Trust or Certification of Trust to identify the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s).

## Step
Eligibility Verification: Determine whether the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are the same.

## Step
Validation and Verification: If they are not the same, obtain and verify written exception by Acra Senior Management.

## Step
Final Determination: Record whether the exception requirement is satisfied or whether no exception is required.

## Deterministic Validation Rules

- If the Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same, written exception by Acra Senior Management has been obtained.

## Outcomes

- **Pass**: The Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are the same, or written exception by Acra Senior Management has been obtained.
- **Conditional**: The Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same and the written exception by Acra Senior Management remains to be obtained.
- **Fail**: The Trustor(s) and Trustee(s) are not the same and written exception by Acra Senior Management has not been obtained.
- **Not Applicable**: Title is not vested in an inter vivos revocable trust.
